payload.name: challenge-axiom-requires-owner
payload.description: Contradiction declarations against axiomatic (entrenchment 1.0) claims by non-owner writers are held for owner review.

payload.statement: Any rewrite of committed history - a flipped bit, or a deleted, inserted, or reordered record - is detected by chain verification.
payload.falsifier: The battery's history attacks pass undetected.

payload.statement: Merkle checkpoints commit to each 1,024-record segment; a segment's root changes if any record it covers changes.
payload.falsifier: A covered record changes without its segment root changing.

payload.statement: The chained store admits exactly one writer; a second concurrent writer is refused.
payload.falsifier: Two writers append to one store concurrently.

payload.statement: A torn final write is truncated at open and reported; damage in the middle of the log is a loud error, never a silent repair.
payload.source: DESIGN-13 section 2.3; kill-point and corruption drills
payload.falsifier: A drill finds a silently repaired middle or a lost torn tail.

payload.statement: The impact query returns a claim's structural dependents and, in propagated mode, the score movement each dependent takes under a hypothetical revision.
payload.source: DESIGN-13 section 3; impact tests and bench
payload.falsifier: A dependent is missing from the closure, or a propagated movement disagrees with re-settlement.

payload.statement: The DESIGN-13 budgets hold on the reference class: append at or above 2,000 records/s, verification at or above 50,000 records/s, open within 250 ms at 100k records.
payload.source: DESIGN-13 section 8; per-PR bench with budgets enforced
payload.falsifier: The bench reports any budget missed.
payload.does_not_establish: Runner-class numbers; not a guarantee on other hardware.

payload.statement: After a checkpoint is anchored, any rewrite of pre-anchor history is detected by consistency verification against the anchored signed tree head.
payload.falsifier: A drill anchors, rewrites history below the anchor, and verification accepts it.
payload.does_not_establish: Proves a history existed and was not rewritten; not that its contents were true.

payload.statement: For any record covered by an anchored checkpoint, an inclusion proof verifies against the anchored root with no access to the store.
payload.falsifier: A standalone verifier accepts a proof for a mutated record, a wrong record, or a wrong checkpoint.

payload.statement: A verifier holding a pinned tree head detects equivocation: two validly signed heads at one tree size with different roots produce a hard fork error.
payload.falsifier: A drill signs two such heads with the real checkpoint key and the verifier accepts both.

payload.statement: No package API path reads from or appends to a partition other than the one opened, and governed verification enforces key enrollment windows.
payload.falsifier: A cross-partition probe succeeds, or a record signed outside its key's window verifies.

payload.statement: Without the tenant's HMAC key, the store's bytes do not yield payload content: a dictionary attack over a known payload space fails against the commitments, while the key holder's recomputation verifies.
payload.falsifier: The drill's keyless attack recovers a payload, or the key holder's recomputation fails.

payload.statement: After an erasure record and destruction of the payload key and salt, the payload is unrecoverable from any ledger artifact, while chain verification, checkpoints, and proofs over the affected region still pass.
payload.falsifier: An erasure drill recovers the payload from the store, a snapshot, or an export.
payload.does_not_establish: An erasure record attests the act was recorded, not that a key was destroyed; destruction happens outside the ledger.

payload.statement: Appends that violate a registered schema version are refused at append time with the violated field named; appends of unregistered types behave exactly as they do today.
payload.source: DESIGN-15 section 6 (stage 3 - not yet built; awaits the Arcturus field-level requirements)
payload.falsifier: The refusal suite accepts a violating append, or a regression run of the existing suite changes behavior.

payload.statement: A disclosure receipt validates for exactly the disclosure record it was issued from - not for another disclosure, another partition, or a mutated record.
payload.source: DESIGN-15 section 6 (stage 3 - not yet built; awaits the Arcturus field-level requirements)
payload.falsifier: A receipt-swap or receipt-mutation drill validates.

payload.statement: The PROV export accounts for the store exactly: every exported activity maps to exactly one ledger record, the export's stated head hash equals the store's, and a re-derived export of an unchanged store is identical.
payload.falsifier: A round-trip accounting test over generated stores finds a mismatch.
payload.does_not_establish: Accounts for the store's records; does not establish the records' contents are true.

payload.statement: A clean environment with no Rust toolchain installs the wheel from the package index and runs the chained-store path end to end: open, migrate, snapshot, verify.
payload.source: DESIGN-15 section 7; PR #49 (stage 5 PR A); every release since 0.14.0
payload.falsifier: The toolchain-scrubbed install smoke fails.

payload.statement: The DESIGN-13 budgets and the full battery, extended per stage, stay green at every release; a stage that cannot keep them does not ship.
payload.source: DESIGN-15 G1; standing, checked at every release
payload.falsifier: A release ships with a red budget or battery leg.

payload.statement: Crash consistency (the prefix property): after a SIGKILL at a random moment, the reopened store verifies cleanly and contains exactly a prefix of the acknowledged appends.
payload.source: DESIGN-16 S1; kill-point sweeps (nightly 500, release tier)
payload.falsifier: The kill-point sweep finds a dropped acknowledged record, a torn middle, or a failed verification.
payload.does_not_establish: Process kills, not power cuts; storage that lies to fsync is out of scope.

payload.statement: Every single-byte corruption of the committed log is detected by verification - exhaustively on the 100-record store, and by 10,000 random flips on the 100k-record store.
payload.falsifier: Either sweep finds an undetected flip.
payload.does_not_establish: Stated as exactly the two sweeps; not a proof over all stores.

payload.statement: Soak stability, as first stated: two hours of mixed load with zero errors and a clean final verification, end-of-run memory drift bounded, and the append leg sustaining the DESIGN-13 append budget of 2,000 appends/s.
payload.falsifier: The soak reports.

payload.statement: Soak stability, first revision: the drift criterion is quiescent retention (RSS after close, garbage collection, and allocator trim), and the mixed and append legs run as separate jobs on separate runners; the append leg sustains the append budget.
payload.source: Soak runs 1-3; PRs #55 and #57 design notes
payload.falsifier: The soak reports.

payload.reason: The first soak runs showed end-of-run RSS measures allocator state, not retention; re-instrumented to quiescent retention and the legs separated.
payload.source: Soak runs 1-3; PRs #55 and #57 design notes

payload.statement: Soak stability: two hours of mixed load with zero errors and a clean final verification, live traced bytes after the run within 25% plus 25 MB of the post-warm-up live level, and a sibling append leg sustaining the full duration with every rotated segment verified, its rate reported as measured; the append budget itself is gated by the per-PR bench.
payload.falsifier: The soak reports.

payload.reason: Four append measurements against the rate gate could not be attributed to the product; the owner re-scoped the gate to the per-PR bench (decision of 2026-10-31), and retention moved to live traced bytes.

payload.statement: Concurrent readers: with 8 reader processes querying during append load, no reader observes a partial or torn record, and point-read latency stays within a p99 of 250 ms.
payload.source: DESIGN-16 S4; PR #50 (point reads); S4 run 2026-10-31 (p99 0.039 ms point reads, 18.457 ms projection)
payload.falsifier: The concurrency run records a torn observation or a p99 above budget.

payload.statement: Resource floors: on a real full disk mid-append, the append fails loudly and the store reopens and verifies at its pre-append state; under a 256 MB memory ceiling, full verification of the 100k-record store completes. Any floor that fails is re-stated at the level actually proven.
payload.source: DESIGN-16 S5; floor legs on every tier run (18,436 appends to genuine ENOSPC, reopen verified at exactly 18,436)
payload.falsifier: The resource-floor runs.

payload.statement: Parser robustness: the fuzz campaigns find zero panics, aborts, or hangs in the fuzzed entry points; any crash found becomes a battery drill before the campaign counts green.
payload.source: DESIGN-16 S6; fuzz legs (nightly and release tier)
payload.falsifier: The campaign reports and their corpora.

payload.statement: Scale point: at 1M records, open within 5 s, full verification at or above 20,000 records/s, structural impact within 250 ms.
payload.source: DESIGN-16 S7; scale run 2026-10-31 (open 2.432 s, verify 65,075 records/s, impact 69.6 ms, median of 5 after warm-up)
payload.falsifier: The nightly scale run misses a number; a miss is revised in the open with the measured number, never quietly edited.
payload.does_not_establish: Runner-class numbers on hosted CI hardware.

payload.statement: The DESIGN-13 budgets and the full battery stay green throughout the stress program; a stress change that costs a budget is a finding, not a trade made silently.
payload.falsifier: A budget or battery leg goes red and the change ships anyway.

payload.statement: Claim fields: a claim carries source, falsifier, and does-not-establish as first-class fields that round-trip through every read path, score revisions, and projection rebuilds.
payload.falsifier: A fielded claim read back with a pattern field missing or altered, at any point in that set.

payload.statement: Append-only corrections: no operation mutates a recorded claim event; a correction is a new event, and the original stands readable as written.
payload.falsifier: A drill whose post-correction log differs anywhere before the correction's own event.

payload.statement: The matrix is generated, never made: every claim in the ledger, live or terminal, appears exactly once, and each row's fields equal the ledger's record for that claim.
payload.falsifier: A generated matrix that omits a claim, duplicates one, or contradicts the live projection on any row.

payload.statement: The map is generated and traceable: headline counts equal the store's own verification counts, and every element carries the ids of the ledger records it rests on.
payload.falsifier: An element with no ledger id, or a headline count that diverges from verification.

payload.statement: The gate regenerates the matrix and the map from the ledger's records and fails on any byte of divergence, naming the diverging layer; it writes nothing.
payload.falsifier: Tamper drills: edit one byte of either artifact, drop a row, or present a stale pair, and the gate passes.
payload.does_not_establish: Proves downstream layers are faithful to the ledger; never that the ledger is faithful to the world.

payload.statement: The engine meets pre-registered expectations on a golden ledger: expectations written from the documented rules before consulting the implementation, reproduced exactly by settlement, impact, and verification.
payload.falsifier: Any golden expectation the engine fails to reproduce.

payload.statement: The pattern module is project-agnostic and ships without breaking the 0.14.0 surface.
payload.source: DESIGN-17 G1; PRs #62 to #66, full CI each
payload.falsifier: A project term appears in the module, or any pre-existing test changes behavior.

payload.label: Re-scope the soak append gate to the bench
payload.rationale: Owner decision, 2026-10-31: the soak append leg proves endurance and integrity; the rate budget is gated by the per-PR bench, whose workload it describes.

payload.label: Release 0.14.0
payload.rationale: Release-tier run 5 fully green on the release commit.

payload.label: Release 0.15.0
payload.rationale: Release-tier run 41311906293 fully green on the tagged commit; tag v0.15.0 published and verified by served identity.
